first_impression.reaction: My assistant read it first, as she always does. Her summary was: a calm, well-sourced guide to weather and paperwork, nothing cheap about it, but nothing that shows they've done a wedding our size. The opening is about cyclone seasons and "the calendar and the paperwork". That's useful to someone choosing a country. It doesn't tell me whether this team can close an island for three days or work with our security. I stopped after the intro. My assistant skimmed on to the venue questions and the closing section to see if it changed.

journey.quote: What separates them for a wedding is the calendar and the paperwork.
journey.reaction: Fair, but for us the calendar and paperwork are things the planner handles. What separates them for us is privacy, access and whether the property can hold everyone. None of that is on the first screen.

journey.quote: Island resorts built around guests who arrive together and stay the week.
journey.reaction: This is the closest the page gets to what we'd need: everyone arriving together and staying the week. My assistant marked it.

journey.quote: If flooding cuts the airport road, how do guests reach the property?
journey.reaction: Good question to ask. It reads like someone who thinks about getting 300 people in and out, not just about the arch on the beach.

journey.quote: A quieter wedding in a modest, predominantly Christian country, where supermarkets cannot sell alcohol from midday Saturday to 7am Monday, though hotels, bars and clubs can.
journey.reaction: Supermarket opening hours have nothing to do with us. It makes the page feel like it's written for people doing the shopping themselves.

journey.quote: Since 5 November, aircraft with more than 30 passenger seats have been barred from Santo International Airport until its rescue and firefighting services are fully running.
journey.reaction: This one matters. We'd charter, so a limit on aircraft size is exactly what my assistant needs to know about.

journey.quote: Curfews and alcohol bans can come at short notice, flights may be suspended with little or no warning, and demonstrations may increase around 13 May, 24 September and elections.
journey.reaction: Honest, and it rules the place out for us straight away. Civil unrest and a family event this visible don't mix. I'd rather know now.

journey.quote: Lagoons and volcanic peaks for a small wedding that runs into a honeymoon.
journey.reaction: "Small wedding" tells me straight away that this isn't written for us. Tahiti could be the place my mother is imagining, and the page has already scaled it down.

journey.quote: A small wedding with a clear legal route in English.
journey.reaction: "Small" again. Twice now the page assumes an intimate guest list. I'm reading it as a guide for a different kind of client.

journey.quote: Which covered room seats every guest if a January or February ceremony is rained out?
journey.reaction: The right question once you're at 300 guests. More of this would have kept me reading.

journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: A single point of contact is good. My assistant would deal with one person, not five. But nothing says they've handled a guest list or a family like ours.

journey.section: Plan your Oceania wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Your Advisor quotes in AUD, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Understated and businesslike, and I appreciate that there's no talk of discounts or packages. It's still about process, though, and says nothing about discretion.

unanswered_questions: Has Wedded Wonderland delivered a wedding of 200 to 400 guests in any of these places?
Can any of these properties be taken for exclusive use, closed to the public for several days?
How does the team handle privacy: NDAs with vendors, no-phone policies for staff, keeping the wedding off social media?
Will the team work alongside our own security and the venue's?
Do they arrange private or charter flights and private transfers for guests between islands?
Can they bring in catering and customs that suit our family, rather than the resort's standard menus?
Is there a private way to make contact, other than a general enquiry form?

turn_offs_found.quote: Lagoons and volcanic peaks for a small wedding that runs into a honeymoon.
turn_offs_found.why: It assumes an intimate wedding. Being treated as a standard client is one of my fears.

turn_offs_found.quote: A small wedding with a clear legal route in English.
turn_offs_found.why: The same assumption again. Read together, the page seems to be for couples with a small guest list.

would_share_with: My assistant, as background reading on seasons and the legal steps, not as a shortlist

cta_reaction.quote: Tell [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=oceania-wedding-destinations&utm_content=closing) which islands are on your list, your month and how many guests are travelling.
cta_reaction.why: I don't enquire through a blog link. We come through a referral or a private introduction. Nothing on this page signals scale, privacy or security, so my assistant has no reason to push for an introduction either. If the page hinted at discretion and large guest lists, she might ask for a private call.

top_3_changes: Add a venue question about exclusive use and working with our own security, so the page shows the team thinks at our scale. Exact edit: old "- If flooding cuts the airport road, how do guests reach the property?" new "- If flooding cuts the airport road, how do guests reach the property?\n- Can the whole property be closed to outside guests for the wedding days, and how would your security work with ours?"

Drop "small" from the Tahiti line so it doesn't scale the wedding down. Exact edit: old "Lagoons and volcanic peaks for a small wedding that runs into a honeymoon." new "Lagoons and volcanic peaks for a wedding that runs into a honeymoon."

Let the closing invitation ask about privacy, which signals discretion without making a claim. Exact edit: old "which islands are on your list, your month and how many guests are travelling." new "which islands are on your list, your month, how many guests are travelling and any privacy or security needs."
